connections.why: Plato gave the four elements the shapes of four regular solids and the cosmos a fifth; the Elements ends by constructing all five and proving there are no more.
Ratdolt's Elements of 1482, printed at Venice a generation after Gutenberg, was the first important mathematical book in print, once he had found a way to print its figures as easily as letters.
Newton laid out the Principia in the Elements' order: definitions, then "axioms, or laws of motion", then propositions proved from them.
Earlier studies of the Antikythera mechanism reached its Venus cycle, 289 in 462 years, by the repeated subtraction that opens Book VII of the Elements, Euclid's algorithm.
